state.stage: Before coding: qualify exactly one aggregate invariant and proposed behavioral RED matrix
state.authority: docs/proposed/contexts/workforce-assurance.md WorkRelationship/WF-01: a rehire is a new work relationship; an ended one stays ended. One identity tenant + normalized worker identifier; one person, worker type and lifecycle. Ended date not before start. Current generic recorded/revised event migration remains outside this slice.
state.observed_candidate: Record active -> Revise at1 to ended -> Revise at2 to active currently has no terminal guard. Existing stale test only rejects old expectedrevision1. Revised reducer retains onlyrevision.
state.boundary: Keep: terminal status and proposed status are facts of the same tenant/worker stream. No cross-owner reads, handlers, reactors, projectors or API changes. Preserve event names, schemas, identities and existing valid date corrections.
state.proposed: Hydrate a monotonic hasEnded flag from either recorded or revised terms with LifecycleStatus ended. Validate existing missing/revision/content gates first. Reject any new non-ended Revise after this stream has ended with StateConflict and no fact. Valid ended-to-ended corrections remain supported. Historical event replay remains readable, including a legacy ended->active history; retain knowledge that it ended for future new decisions. Exact original Record retry after end remains successful without a new fact; changed registration intent still conflicts.
red_matrix: Ended via Revise -> valid pending/active/on_leave current-revision transitions refuse with StateConflict, unchanged revision and no additional fact; exercise direct state and JSON-replayed owner.
Initially recorded ended -> same refusals so both event reducers hydrate terminal state.
Ended -> ended date correction remains allowed, including after replay.
Original registration exact retry after end is success without a fact; changed intent conflicts.
Legacy ended->active event history remains readable; a new nonended revision remains refused.
Stale revision failure retains precedence; rehydrated loser of ending decision cannot reactivate.
state.completion_boundary: This is terminal-lifecycle hardening only. The whole target aggregate stays partial for named lifecycle facts, remaining target identity/worker-type rules, authoritative sponsor qualification and framework physical append qualification.

local_owner.instructions: Can this stream decide that a new revision would reactivate an ended relationship using only its own recorded/revised facts?

criteria.true: Its own historical terms establish ending and the proposed terms provide the requested status, so the terminal rule is local and atomic.
criteria.false: Authoritative ending status requires another owner or a projection, so this stream alone cannot decide.

keep_terminal_history.instructions: Does retaining a monotonic fact that the relationship has ended preserve WF-01 while permitting historical replay and future ended-date corrections?

criteria.true: A prior ended fact remains known even if legacy history reactivated it; replay is not rejected, and a valid proposed ended status still permits correction.
criteria.false: The flag erases required historical facts or necessarily blocks valid ended-date corrections.

bounded_red_matrix.instructions: Does the listed matrix exercise the terminal-status decision plus its recorded/revised hydration, original registration retries and valid correction boundaries?

criteria.true: The cases cover current expected revision, all nonended statuses, both reducer origins, replay, no facts on refusal, correction and retry precedence.
criteria.false: A concrete listed decision boundary is not exercised or the plan primarily tests handler/API behavior instead.
